analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the rebound held through the open — S&P +1.0%, Nasdaq +1.6%, Dow +0.5% as of 9:31 AM ET, with the Nasdaq leading on the Anthropic-debut AI revival. Two corrections to the premarket read: (1) Walmart's Q3 actually BEAT on both lines (revenue $188.8B, adj EPS $0.65 vs $0.64) with raised full-year guidance — the 6 AM 'narrowly missed' line came from an early Investopedia read that other outlets (Morningstar, AP) contradict; shares are down ~3% anyway, so the market is selling the beat on slowing comps (2.9% vs 4.5% a year ago). (2) The Apple iPhone order-cut story is not fresh — the Nikkei report dates to Oct 9; AAPL is the lone Mag 7 decliner again (-1.1% early) but there is no new Apple headline today. Nvidia is rebounding ~1.3% premarket after Wednesday's -2.9% close erased the whole post-earnings gain; the record quarter (rev $115.84B, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47, Q4 guide $130B) still loses the argument to the leadership vacuum and a wave of price-target cuts. Fed Vice Chair Jefferson's fresh remarks frame the AI buildout as inflationary now, with productivity gains only 'in the future' — and he said nothing about rates, leaving the December 25bp hike ~90-95% priced. The 8:30 AM ET data (claims 203K, Philly Fed 6.3) is now confirmed by multiple outlets, upgrading the 6 AM single-source flag. Signal vs noise: the index rebound, the WMT beat-vs-selloff, Jefferson's framing, and the NVDA target cuts are signal; the exact size of early Mag 7 moves and the ANT opening print (expected ~noon-1pm ET) are noise until the session confirms them.

community_signals.takeaway: The 922-comment Anthropic IPO thread remains the live debate on the day's center of gravity, now reframed by the confirmed $83 price and the $26B supplier private placement: 'priced for perfection' skepticism at ~$1.5T vs AI-scarcity enthusiasm. It frames how the market may read ANT's first trade (~noon-1pm ET).

headlines.headline: Rebound holds through the open: S&P 500 +1.01% to 7,397.35, Nasdaq Composite +1.55% to 24,809.76, Dow +0.47% to 50,433.9 as of 9:31 AM ET (BestStocks/FMP). VIX ~22.39, down ~2.2 points from Wednesday's 24.56 close. 10-year Treasury ~5.09%. If the S&P holds, it ends a five-day losing streak.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket pop survived the opening bell rather than fading — breadth into the close will show whether this is a durable turn or a relief rally into the Anthropic debut.

headlines.headline: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said Thursday the AI buildout is putting upward pressure on US inflation through demand, with possible productivity gains only coming 'in the future' (Reuters, prepared remarks to a Brazilian central bank conference). He did not mention his interest-rate outlook. The Fed is expected to raise 25bp from 3.75%-4.00% at its Dec 8-9 meeting; markets price ~90-95% for a 25bp hike, ~10% for 50bp.
headlines.why_it_matters: Jefferson frames the AI boom as inflationary now and disinflationary later — that keeps the hawkish December-hike case intact, and his silence on rates means the market gets no dovish offset today.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) first trade expected around noon-1pm ET today on the Nasdaq, after pricing its IPO at $83 a share — above the $70-78 range — in an $81B offering, the largest on record, for a ~$1.5T valuation. The $26B private placement at $83 was bought by seven suppliers (Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom $1B, Micron $1B, Microsoft $1B, TSMC $0.5B). 315M insider shares are eligible to sell from day one.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still the day's center of gravity — the first trade prices whether the AI supply chain buying its biggest customer's equity is partnership or circularity, and day-one insider supply is a real overhang.

headlines.headline: Correction to the 6 AM read: Walmart's Q3 actually BEAT — revenue $188.8B (+5.2% YoY) vs ~$187.3B expected, adjusted EPS $0.65 vs $0.64 expected — and it raised full-year guidance to $2.84-2.89 (from $2.80-2.87). Shares are down ~3% early anyway ($123.45 at 9:31 AM ET). U.S. comps slowed to 2.9% vs 4.5% a year ago and net income fell 19.5% YoY.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise that still sells off — the market is grading slowing comps and the profit line, not the top line, into the holidays. The 6 AM 'narrowly missed' line was wrong; the print beat.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) rebounding ~1.3% premarket after Wednesday's -2.9% close to $150.96 erased the entire post-earnings gain. The record Q3 (revenue $115.84B, +103% YoY; EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected; Q4 guide $130B vs ~$125.1B) still loses to the leadership question: Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12, interim CEO Colette Kress leads, and analysts keep cutting targets — UBS to $220 (from $240), Jefferies to $250 (from $300), Mizuho to $220 (from $250), Morgan Stanley to $260 (from $267), Piper to $230 (from $300).
headlines.why_it_matters: The quarter answered the demand question; the market is now asking the leadership and valuation questions — the premarket bounce is a test of whether $150 holds as a floor.

headlines.headline: Mag 7 early session: Microsoft +3.04% to $523.75 (Stifel upgrade — 'getting back on track' — plus Anthropic private-placement buyer), Alphabet +~4% premarket (strongest of the group), Meta +1.47% to $625.46, Amazon +~2.1% premarket, Tesla +0.58% to $385.94. Apple is the lone decliner at -1.09% to $348.60 — but note the iPhone 18 Pro order-cut report is from Oct 9, not fresh news today; there is no new Apple headline.
headlines.why_it_matters: Six of seven Mag 7 names are green in the cash session — the rebound is broad, not just futures. Apple remains the divergence, and its drag is a stale demand story, not a new one.

headlines.headline: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) carried from premarket: beat-and-raise — fiscal Q1 revenue $3.445B (+39% YoY) vs ~$3.31B expected, adjusted EPS $1.05 vs $0.97, Next-Generation Security ARR +66%; FY27 revenue guide lifted to $14.52-14.57B and non-GAAP EPS to $4.26-4.30; also a $4.5B acquisition of Applied Compute. CrowdStrike +12% premarket in sympathy.
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean beat-and-raise with a lifted full-year guide is the strongest earnings catalyst — and it is lifting the whole cybersecurity sector, not just PANW.

headlines.headline: 8:30 AM ET data now confirmed by multiple outlets (upgraded from single-source at 6 AM): initial jobless claims 203K for the week ending Nov 14, slightly above the ~197-198K forecast; continuing claims 1.763M. Philly Fed manufacturing index printed 6.3 vs ~20.6 expected and 20.9 prior — a sharp downside miss.
headlines.why_it_matters: Claims are DOL-confirmed and still near historic lows, which keeps the hawkish frame intact; the Philly Fed miss is now corroborated, so it reads as a genuinely soft manufacturing print against the rate-hike case.
